summary: Checks ordinary List elements against one homogeneous defaulted type or one exact declared target, including an explicit closed union; direct suffix-free atomic numeric literals may adopt an exact numeric target, and the predicate never synthesizes a Union.
requires: the literal constructs immutable List<T> and is never context-rewritten to NumericArray
every scanner-admitted suffix-free numeric token is validated once by NumericLiteralAdmitted; '-' remains a separate AST prefix operator
without context, integer, real, and imaginary/complex atoms default only to Int, Float64, and Complex<Float64>; an empty literal is not inferable and all normalized element types must be identical

with a fixed contextual List<T>, a nonnumeric element's normalized type must equal T exactly; assignment compatibility, subtype conversion, variance, hidden conversion, clone, ownership weakening, Option insertion, and source-order preference do not count as equality
with a fixed contextual List<T>, a direct atomic numeric literal is delegated with exact T and admits exactly as T iff representable, including ISize, USize, Float32, and Float64 targets
with fixed exact signed Int, IntN, or ISize target T, only direct PrefixExpr(-, IntegerLiteral) may request a magnitude fact and form signed candidate -magnitude; an in-range candidate admits as T

a negative prefix expression under an exact unsigned UInt, UIntN, or USize target is rejected before the signed adapter with UINT_NEGATIVE_CONTEXT_ADAPTER_FORBIDDEN; an out-of-range signed candidate, including Int8 -129, emits LIST_LITERAL_CONTEXT_INTEGER_OUT_OF_RANGE
the prefix-sign adapter performs no arbitrary constant folding, hidden widening, or expression rewrite
a candidate carrying any removed numeric type suffix is rejected by the scanner with NUMERIC_TYPE_SUFFIX_REMOVED before token/CST/AST/HIR creation or predicate invocation
there is no source-suffix, smallest-fit, implicit unsigned/BigInt/platform, width-fit, integer/float, signed/unsigned, width-changing, nominal, union, or source-order-dependent inference or join

reject a negative prefix expression under UInt, UIntN, or USize before entering the adapter with UINT_NEGATIVE_CONTEXT_ADAPTER_FORBIDDEN; emit LIST_LITERAL_CONTEXT_INTEGER_OUT_OF_RANGE only for an unrepresentable signed-adapter candidate; do not fold any other expression or insert conversion
